title: install skill --yes at project scope writes the skill, its manifest and the relative link
source: intended: docs: B4B5-DESIGN.md B4-13 to B4-15, c.2
intent: INTENDED behavior (defect N-16, B4.3). `--yes` creates `.agents/skills/jitso/SKILL.md` (frontmatter starts `name: jitso` then `description: `), `references/README.md` and the manifest `.jitso-skill.json` (`v`, `skill`, `jitso_version`, a 64 hex `content_sha256`, one SHA-256 per file), and the link `.claude/skills/jitso` so the skill is also reachable through `.claude/skills/jitso/SKILL.md`. It prints one line per action and `jitso install skill: done`, and a note to commit both paths (the paths are untracked). A fresh install needs no backup. That the link is a symbolic link with the relative target is pinned by a Go unit test, because a file check follows links. The oracle has no `install` command: it answers `unknown command "install"` on stderr with exit 2 and prints nothing on stdout, so the pinned output and file effects FAIL on it.

stdout: note: commit .agents/skills/jitso and .claude/skills/jitso so other clones get the skill
